title: How Election Workers Make Sure Votes Are Counted Right
summary:
The midterm elections end on Election Day in November, but people in many states are already voting. Election workers started getting ready even earlier.

In Davis County, Utah, workers put practice ballots through the counting machines before any real ballots are counted. Some practice ballots are filled out wrong on purpose. This test checks that the machines count correctly and catch mistakes, like a voter picking too many candidates.

Most people in Utah vote by mail. County clerk Brian McKenzie explained that every envelope has its own bar code, so no one can get more than one ballot. Two workers pick up returned ballots, and cameras watch them all day and night. Workers check each voter's signature, and ballots are counted again at every step. McKenzie said nothing is connected to the internet.

This year, there was a fight in Washington over voting by mail. The Supreme Court blocked new mail ballot rules last month. McKenzie said sudden changes close to an election can confuse voters.
why_it_matters: Knowing how votes are checked helps kids understand how their families' choices are counted fairly in elections.

background_read: In the United States, local officials in each county run elections and count the votes.
Before Election Day, workers test the counting machines and check mail ballots carefully so every vote counts only once.
